title: How he extended the bass range, working on it since 1937
summary: He began developing high notes around 1937, inspired by Ray Perry's violin, and keeps the method secret; he adds comedy at the end.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Right. Well, maybe, before -- let's see, we're almost at the end of this tape. Maybe after dinner, we could get you playing a little bit of this, put it on the tape. Is that all right with you?
Sure, all right.
Because that'll put -- I mean, that'll -- yeah, I think we'd get that on there.
That would be great, yeah, love to.
So now, how long have you been working on this expansion of the range of bass?
Oh, I've been working on that, I'd say, oh, many, many, many years. It might go back to -- oh, let's say, 1937.
You started working on that 42 years ago?
Yes, that's for sure.
How did you come to the -- how did you -- I'm getting tongue-tied, I'm so staggered by this. How did you come to working on that? I mean, because there's nothing that I know of that --
Yes. Well, what might have gave me the idea was being with the -- if you remember, the young saxophone violinist I told you about, Ray Perry?
Right, uh-huh.

That's where I really actually -- it came to me all of a sudden. "Why can't I make my fiddle sound, my bass fiddle, sound like a little violin?" It was one of those spur of the moment thoughts that I came across. So I tried to -- eventually I figured out a way to make these high notes on my bass fiddle, which is more or less a secret.
Well, I'm not interested in how you did it.
(Laughter.)
All right.
I mean, even if I was, I shouldn't find
find out.

So I climbed up on my top string and I found that as I went along, I was very successful in doing this thing. So I've been doing this thing all of these years and I'm still trying to reach that higher notes, as I go along, you know.
So you've been able to add like -- you've been able to add more -- you've been able to get further and you've been able to go higher in the range over the years?
Well, not too much higher. But every once in a while, I go a little higher than that squeak D.
Oh.
Then, of course, at the end of it, I make -- I do a little comedy with it also, which enhances it, I believe. It's quite a little thing that I discovered. I kept it in, you know.
It would seem to me that a lot of bass players would have taken notice of that right off the bat.
It seems to be that way, but I haven't heard anybody do it or attempt it.
